statement: The special Euclidean group $\mathrm{SE}(3)$ (also denoted $\mathrm{E}^+(3)$) is the Lie group of direct Euclidean isometries (rigid motions) of three-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{E}^3$ that preserve Euclidean distance and handedness, comprising arbitrary combinations of translations and rotations without reflections, with semidirect product structure $\mathrm{E}^+(3) = \mathrm{SO}(3) \ltimes \mathrm{T}(3)$ where $\mathrm{SO}(3) \cong \mathrm{E}^+(3)/\mathrm{T}(3)$.

symbols.meaning: special Euclidean group in dimension 3 (group of direct isometries / rigid motions)
translational normal subgroup of translations in 3 dimensions
special orthogonal group of direct orthogonal transformations with determinant 1

properties.property: SE(3) has 6 degrees of freedom, with 3 degrees of freedom attributed to translational symmetry and 3 to rotational symmetry.
properties.why: Evaluated from n(n + 1)/2 with n = 3 translational and n(n - 1)/2 rotational degrees of freedom

properties.property: SE(3) is a subgroup of index 2 in E(3).
properties.why: Indirect isometries form a single coset E-(3) of E+(3)

properties.property: E+(3) has semidirect product structure SO(3) ⋉ T(3), or equivalently T(3) ⋊ SO(3), with SO(3) ≅ E+(3)/T(3).
properties.why: T(3) is a normal subgroup and elements are uniquely an orthogonal transformation with determinant 1 and a translation

properties.property: SE(3) is a connected Lie group.
properties.why: Any two direct isometries can be connected by a continuous trajectory in E+(3) and calculus notions adapt directly

properties.property: Elements can be explicitly represented either by a pair (A, b) where A is a 3 × 3 orthogonal matrix with determinant 1 and b is a real column vector of size 3 acting by x ↦ Ax + c (or x ↦ A(x + b)), or by a single square matrix of size 4.
properties.why: SE(3) is a subgroup of the affine group respecting the semidirect product structure

properties.property: Any element of E+(3) is a screw displacement.
properties.why: Asserted by Chasles' theorem for direct isometries in three dimensions

assumptions.assumption: Transformations are direct Euclidean isometries preserving Euclidean distance and orientation/handedness in 3D Euclidean space
assumptions.breaks_when: Transformations include reflections (indirect isometries) or non-isometric operations such as scaling or shearing

failure_modes.signature: det(A) = -1 or handedness of chiral figures is reversed
failure_modes.cause: Applying a reflection places the isometry in the coset E-(3) rather than the special Euclidean subgroup SE(3)
